acceptance_review.finding: Decision 0065 and SPEC rule 17 require explicit documentation impact or justified no-impact before completion; silence is rejected.
Documentation closure remains distinct from F-016 parity, WI044 evidence sufficiency, and WI046 admission.
Decision 0065 compares work-item, criterion, evidence, and mapping layers and defines source of truth, lifecycle, migration, and compatibility.
The mechanism classifies the required documentation surfaces without prescribing adopter paths; adopter-neutral fixture uses a different layout.
A no-impact outcome requires a reviewable rationale and does not force meaningless documentation edits.
Affected mappings identify source and documentation paths and require evidence linkage; generic docs-updated text is insufficient.
Optional owners.json mappings bind source and documentation paths and compare structural digests without claiming prose-semantic proof.
Generated outputs are mapped and stale output is detected against source digests; generators are not run silently.
Both Rust and Python completion validation reject unresolved documentation impact at the completed transition.
Doctor and audit surface stale mappings read-only; the dedicated test verifies governance records remain unchanged.
Conformance includes positive, no-impact, missing-resolution, absent-evidence, stale-source, and stale-generated-output cases.
ForgeWire-shaped and adopter-neutral fixtures pass; the genericity claim is falsified if a different adopter layout cannot opt in, or if source-only/output-only/paired drift is misclassified.

Decision 0076 fixes schema version 1 and optional configuration before implementation; repositories without the optional mapping remain valid and historical completed work is not retroactively rewritten.
Schema, Rust/Python validation, CLI, templates, SPEC, workflow, doctor/audit, reporting, fixtures, conformance, and regression tests are present and covered by current-main validation.
